name: Vanta
tagline: Automated compliance monitoring and audit prep for SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and friends.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Vanta sells annual contracts through sales, so public numbers are unreliable.

verdictSummary: The software part of Vanta is a checklist, a pile of integration pollers, and a policy template library, and yes, an agent can rough that out. The part you are actually buying is that an auditor accepts the evidence and a procurement team accepts the trust report. Nobody closes an enterprise deal by pointing at a SQLite dashboard you wrote on a Sunday. Frameworks also drift, auditor expectations drift, and keeping the control mappings current is a full time job for a compliance team, not a cron script. Build the evidence tracker if you want to know where you stand before paying someone, then pay someone.
coreLoopDIY: A local control checklist mapped to SOC 2 criteria that pulls read-only facts from AWS, GitHub and Google Workspace, stores evidence snapshots, and prints a gap report.
requirements: Read-only API tokens for AWS, GitHub and Google Workspace in .env
Someone willing to write the actual policy documents
An actual licensed auditor if you ever want a report that counts
whatYouLose: The audit itself: your dashboard is not an opinion from a CPA firm
A trust center page that buyers and procurement teams already recognize
Framework mappings maintained by people who track control changes for a living
Dozens of maintained integrations, plus personnel tracking, background checks and vendor reviews
The vendor security questionnaire workflow, which is most of the day to day value
moatNotes: Compliance tooling is unusual: the buyer is not the user, the buyer is an auditor and a stranger's procurement team.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the deal is blocked. Somebody in a large company said no SOC 2, no contract, and the fastest path from there to a signed report runs through a vendor that already has auditor relationships, evidence collectors that auditors trust, and a report page you can link in a sales email. The price looks absurd next to the actual code, and it is, but it is small next to the revenue that is waiting on the checkbox. Nobody wants to argue with an auditor about their homegrown evidence pipeline.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend; the signature at the bottom of the report is not. The moat is compliance and regulation: auditor acceptance and the fact that your customer's procurement team has heard of Vanta and not of you.
prompt:
Build a local-only compliance readiness tracker. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, not negotiable:
- TypeScript, Node 20
- Next.js App Router with a single local dev server
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/compliance.db
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Secrets in .env only, .env.example committed, .env gitignored

Data model:
- controls: id, framework, criterion (e.g. CC6.1), title, description, owner, status (not-started, in-progress, met, not-applicable), notes
- evidence: id, control_id, collected_at, source, summary, raw_json
- checks: id, name, control_ids (json array), collector key, last_run_at, last_result (pass, fail, error), detail

Seed the controls table from a committed JSON file with a hand written SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria outline covering security, availability and confidentiality. Mark clearly in the file header that this is an unofficial outline, not an audit program.

Write three read-only collectors as separate modules, each behind a token in .env, each skipping cleanly with a warning if its token is missing:
1. GitHub: for a given org, list repos and report branch protection on default branches, plus whether 2FA is required for the org
2. AWS: list IAM users without MFA, S3 buckets with public access blocks disabled, and whether CloudTrail is enabled in the configured region
3. Google Workspace (Admin SDK): list users and whether 2SV is enforced

Each collector writes an evidence row with a raw JSON snapshot and updates the linked check result. Never write, never delete, never assume rights beyond read.

CLI: `npm run collect` runs all available collectors, `npm run report` writes ./out/gap-report.md listing every control with status, owner, latest evidence date, and a flagged list of controls with zero evidence.

UI: one page listing controls grouped by criterion with inline status and owner editing, one control detail page showing evidence history, one page listing checks with last run and result.

Out of scope, do not build: policy generation, employee onboarding, vendor questionnaires, a public trust page, PDF export, multi-user auth.

README must state plainly that this tool tells you where you stand and does not produce an audit report, and that a licensed auditor is still required.
